plans.rationale: This is the first round of investigation for INC-03. We need to establish the symptom onset and error rates for the reported symptomatic services (payments-api, mobile-bff) using observability, and simultaneously check recent changes, dependency maps, and external integrations (specifically upi-gateway and external npci-switch or partner-bank-api) using the dependency agent.

tasks.goal: Check error rates, latency p99, and logs for payments-api and mobile-bff to determine exact symptom onset and identify downstream failing dependencies.

Review recent deployments, configuration changes, feature flags, and infrastructure events across all services, and inspect the dependency graph around payments-api, upi-gateway, and external payment providers.
Check error rates, latency p99, and logs for payments-api and mobile-bff to determine exact symptom onset and identify downstream failing dependencies.

Review recent deployments, configuration changes, feature flags, and infrastructure events across all services, and inspect the dependency graph around payments-api, upi-gateway, and external payment providers.
Build and rank competing root-cause hypotheses

r1-observability-1.summary: Investigation into payments-api and mobile-bff shows that payments-api latency and error rates began increasing at 13:45 due to timeouts calling upi-gateway (POST /v2/collect). upi-gateway in turn is experiencing worker pool exhaustion and high latency because its downstream dependency partner-bank-api shows latency and error rate spikes starting at 13:41.

findings.statement: payments-api latency p99 spiked significantly starting at 2026-10-04T13:45:00+00:00, reaching over 10s.
payments-api error rate increased starting at 2026-10-04T13:47:00+00:00, reaching nearly 11-12%.
mobile-bff error rate increased starting at 2026-10-04T13:47:00+00:00, mirroring the payments-api failure.
payments-api logs show continuous 10000ms timeouts calling upi-gateway POST /v2/collect beginning at 13:46:00.
upi-gateway latency p99 began rising at 13:43:00 and error rate began rising at 13:46:00.
upi-gateway experienced worker pool exhaustion due to requests waiting on partner-bank-api.
partner-bank-api latency p99 spiked starting at 13:41:00 and its error rate increased starting at 13:45:00, preceding the symptoms in upi-gateway and payments-api.

open_questions: What specific internal issue or load increase occurred within partner-bank-api at 13:41 to trigger the latency spike?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency paths and gathered all recent configuration changes and deployments prior to INC-03. payments-api relies synchronously on upi-gateway, ledger-service, fraud-service, and redis-cache. upi-gateway calls external npci-switch and partner-bank-api. Relevant changes prior to symptom onset at ~13:45 include orders-service v1.25.0, ledger-service v6.7.0, and a fraud-service rules config change.

findings.statement: payments-api has synchronous dependencies on upi-gateway, ledger-service, fraud-service, redis-cache, and asynchronous on event-bus.
upi-gateway depends synchronously on external npci-switch and partner-bank-api.
fraud-service velocity threshold configuration was raised from 5 to 7 transactions/min at 2026-10-04T13:30:00+00:00.

open_questions: Are external network timeouts occurring at the npci-switch or partner-bank-api level?
Did the ledger-service or fraud-service updates impact transaction response times leading to the timeouts reported at ~13:45?

hypotheses.title: External Partner Bank Latency Spike
hypotheses.mechanism: External partner-bank-api experienced degradation and latency starting at 13:41, causing synchronous callers upi-gateway and payments-api to block, exhaust worker pools, and timeout on requests.

supporting.note: Shows the earliest anomaly onset at 13:41 preceding all other service latencies.
Shows upi-gateway latency rising immediately after partner-bank-api at 13:43.
Shows upi-gateway worker pool exhaustion with workers waiting on partner-bank-api.
Shows payments-api latency jumping at 13:45 mirroring downstream delays.

assumptions: The root cause inside partner-bank-api is entirely external and outside internal system logs.

hypotheses.title: UPI Gateway Worker Pool Concurrency Bottleneck
hypotheses.mechanism: A strict concurrency limit or internal resource exhaustion inside upi-gateway amplified latency and caused timeouts independent of external partner behavior.

supporting.note: Confirms worker pool exhaustion (200/200 busy) on upi-gateway.

contradicting.note: Partner-bank-api latency started rising at 13:41, whereas upi-gateway metrics only started rising at 13:43, proving the fault originated upstream.

assumptions: upi-gateway worker pool limits were set too low for normal operation.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The onset of symptoms is established at 2026-10-04T13:41:00+00:00 when partner-bank-api latency began rising ([metric:partner-bank-api:latency_p99_ms]). This directly preceded the upi-gateway latency anomaly at 13:43 ([metric:upi-gateway:latency_p99_ms]), worker pool exhaustion at 13:47 ([log-00742]), and payments-api timeouts starting at 13:45 ([metric:payments-api:latency_p99_ms], [log-00698]). Hypothesis H1 accurately captures this upstream failure chain with high confidence, while H2 remains a weak alternative.

adjustments.reason: Direct evidence from telemetry shows partner-bank-api latency spiking first at 13:41, followed precisely by upi-gateway worker pool exhaustion and payments-api timeouts. The causal chain is complete and well-supported.
Alternative hypothesis is contradicted by the clear upstream latency onset at partner-bank-api occurring before upi-gateway worker exhaustion.
